justification: A has a dark cover, a table of contents with dot leaders, a top rule on each page, and a consistent serif heading hierarchy. Its image is placed beside text on A4, so pages stay filled. B has no TOC, and its image page (B3) is mostly empty. B4 opens with a large gap above the heading. B's headings are bold sans and clear, but its heading indents are inconsistent, with headings sitting outside the text margin. A's text blocks are well proportioned and its pages are more even.

A sets 'History' in a navy band heading with clearly distinct subheads, giving stronger hierarchy than B's numbered headings. A's text flows continuously and fills pages 2-4, with no dead space. B leaves large gaps on A2-equivalent B2 and a nearly empty B5 with a few lines, which breaks rhythm and balance. B's serif body is pleasant, but its page flow is weaker. Both put the photo on its own page, so imagery is equal.

A's serif body is comfortable to read, with clear numbered headings (1 Precursors, 1.1, 1.2) and a thin running header (A3, A4). B has a heavier navy header band and a Precursors banner, but its condensed sans body is denser, its headings are weaker, and the Precursors banner is stranded at the foot of B2 with its text split across the page break. A's last page is nearly empty apart from a broken image markdown line (A5), a flaw that B shares at the foot of B4, though B's pages fill more evenly. Overall A reads better.

A has a navy header band on each page and a filled banner for the Precursors heading. It also keeps subheadings clearly weighted and fills its pages evenly. B uses a thin running header and numbered headings, which look plain and are less distinct. B also leaves page B5 almost empty apart from a stray broken image line. Both designs show the same broken image markdown, but A's page 4 has it as the last line of an otherwise full page, so it hurts less. B's serif body text is comfortable to read, but A's overall structure is stronger.

B flows continuously across pages with no near-empty page, and it has a strong banded History heading (B2) that gives clear hierarchy. A leaves page 5 mostly blank (A5) after a short text spill, and its headings are numbered but plain. B's image page is slightly larger and more prominent (B5). A's serif body is pleasant and readable, but its pagination is weaker.

A places the honeycomb image with its heading and text on one page (A4) and fills pages evenly, ending on a full-page bee photo (A7). The serif heading hierarchy is elegant and the thin top rule is quiet. B strands the image on a mostly empty page (B4) and leaves several half-empty pages (B7, B8). Its navy header and footer bands are heavy, though the section divider (B5) is a bold touch and the numbered headings are clear.

A pairs a serif body with sans headings, and its drop caps give a refined, book-like feel (A2-A4). Its heading levels are clear and its text blocks are comfortable to read. However, A5 is almost empty, and the drop-cap sections leave uneven gaps, which hurts rhythm and balance. B is dense and consistent, with header and footer bands and a solid History banner (B2). But it is a plain sans throughout, with tightly packed text, and its heavy bands add clutter. B flows continuously with no stranded pages, which is its main advantage. A's typographic quality outweighs that.

B flows continuously with consistent running header and footer bands, numbered headings, and a full-width image. A is fragmented: sections are forced onto separate pages, leaving large empty areas (A2, A4, A6). Its indentation is inconsistent, drop caps break awkwardly, and the lead paragraphs are set in a different size. B's headings are more uniform and the page rhythm is steadier. A's heading typography is attractive, but its layout is choppy.

A has a navy header band with running titles and a filled 'Precursors' band, so its section structure is clearer (A2). Its footers are clean and its pages are filled evenly. B's serif body text is comfortable to read, but the 'Precursors' heading sits oddly with a rule above and an indented intro (B3), and the last page is mostly empty (B5). Both show the same broken image markdown text (A4, B5).

A has bold sans headings with numbered sections, clear header and footer bands showing the section name, and justified body text that reads easily (A2-A5). The image is placed right under its section opener with a caption (A3). B has weak hierarchy: light, similar-looking headings, and an oversized lead paragraph under each heading that competes with the body text. B also has odd rules, a section heading stranded at the bottom of page 2, and a thin top line instead of real header bands (B2-B5). Both show the same broken image markdown text, so that does not separate them.

B has clearer hierarchy: bold sans-serif numbered headings (1 Precursors, 1.1 Second millennium BCE) set against a serif body, plus running headers showing the current section and 'Page X of 5' footers. A's headings are weak: 'Precursors' is set large in regular weight, like body text. A's top rule and footer are tidy but do less to orient the reader. B's cover is a lighter navy with a bold sans title and reads well. Both share the broken image markdown on the last page and large empty areas there. B's body text is slightly larger and easier to read.

A has a consistent system: navy running header and footer bands, solid section banners and uniform body text, with the image sitting well on A3 (page 3). B is inconsistent: section headings are outdented against indented body text, and lead paragraphs are set at different sizes. Its drop caps misalign with the text that follows them (B4, B5), there are large empty gaps at the tops of pages (B4, B6), and the cover is plainer. Both leave the broken image markdown visible, and A's page 5 ends with a large empty area.

B has a running header band and footer on every page, and a filled banner for the Precursors heading, so it feels more structured and consistent. Its page flow is continuous and the broken image markdown sits inside the text on B4. A's serif body is pleasant, but A5 is almost empty apart from the raw image markdown, A2 has no running header, and A has uneven page fill and heading treatment (a rule above Precursors on A3 only).

A keeps a consistent running header and footer band, numbered headings, and continuous text flow that fills the pages evenly (A2-A5). The image sits well within the text on A3. B has headings that are misaligned with the indented body text, drop caps that break the line alignment, and mixed body sizes (B3, B4, B5). B also leaves large empty areas on B3, B4 and B6 from forced page breaks. Both designs show the same broken image markdown, so that flaw does not separate them.

A pairs a serif body with a geometric sans heading, which reads comfortably, and gives sections clear rules and bold headings (A2, A4, A5). Its margins are generous and the pages flow well. B has a striking section divider with a sidebar band (B4) and header/footer bands, but the bands add clutter. B's body text is denser and its headings are weaker; the Etymology heading is light (B2). B also leaves a nearly empty page (B7) and a half-empty page after the divider, so its rhythm is uneven. A has some empty areas too (A3, A4 top), but they are milder.

A pairs a serif title with a dark navy cover and a top rule on each page. Its body text is airy and its headings are refined, with a larger lead paragraph on A3 that reads as an intro. B uses a sans heading with a serif body, and its headings sit slightly outdented. B's justified text shows wider word gaps and tighter lines, and its running footer is cluttered. Both show the same broken image markdown on page 5, so neither gains there.

B adds a table of contents (B2), running header and footer bands (B3), and a bold section divider with a sidebar (B5). Together these give clearer navigation and structure. A is clean, with a nice large-image page (A7), but it is plainer: its headings are inconsistent, and a large empty gap above the heading on A4 breaks its rhythm. B has some empty pages (B4, B8) and its numbered headings are slightly weaker than A's bold ones, but overall it reads as the more complete, professional document.

A has a navy band for the History heading, running header and footer bands, and bold sans subheads, so sections are easy to find (A2, A3). B's serif body is elegant, but its headings are weak and only a thin rule marks the break, so it reads as one long uniform text (B2, B3). Both give the photo similar treatment (A5, B5), and A's cover is slightly crisper (A1).

Design B has clear running header and footer bands and solid section banners, and its content flows continuously from page to page. Its image is large and well integrated (B3). Design A leaves large empty areas, with a section header floating at the top of nearly empty pages (A3, A4, A6). A's mixed body sizes and drop caps are inconsistent, and the image page is half empty (A3). A's elegant serif and drop caps are attractive but do not offset the uneven page rhythm.

A uses a bold sans for numbered headings against a serif body, so the section structure is clear (A3, A4). It also has running headers and 'Page x of 5' footers. B's headings are light and weak, and 'Precursors' has an odd rule above it with a larger intro paragraph (B3). B's body text is thin and small, with wide line spacing. B also breaks a sentence across pages (B4 to B5). Both show the same broken image markdown on the last page and a mostly empty page, so neither gains there (A5, B5).

B has a running header band and a filled section band that give clear navigation (B2-B4). Its pages fill evenly, with no stranded page. A's serif body is elegant and its heading hierarchy is clear, but page A5 is nearly empty apart from a broken image markdown line. A has a thin top rule only, and pages A2 and A3 end with uneven white gaps. Both share the broken image text, though B's is less isolated.

A uses filled navy section bands, running header and footer bars, and bold sans subheads. The levels are easy to tell apart and the pages are easy to scan (A2, A3, A4). B's serif body is elegant, but its section headings are light and oversized, and the lead paragraph under each heading is set larger than the body text. That makes B's hierarchy feel inconsistent (B2, B3, B5). Both leave a broken image-markdown line, and A's last page is half empty, but B's pages are similarly sparse.

B adds a table of contents (B2) and numbered headings (B3, B6, B7), so the structure is easier to follow. Its serif body text with a sans heading pairing reads comfortably (B3, B6). The running header in B also repeats the numbered section name. A's sans-serif body is light and tight, with inconsistent justification and a header that says 'Etymology and name' on the intro page (A2). A also has unnumbered headings, a mostly empty page 7 and an awkward image placement on A8. B shares the large empty areas on B4 and B8, and its divider page is similar to A's, though with a numeral that adds hierarchy (B5).

A has a fuller document structure: a table of contents (A2), running header and footer bands with page numbers, and a bold section divider page (A5) with a sidebar. Numbered headings give a clearer hierarchy. A also leaves large empty areas, such as the image-only page A4 and the half-empty A8, and it stops before the second image. B is simpler and more uniform, with a bold geometric heading font, and it includes the second bee photo (B7). However, its headings are weaker, it has no bands or contents page, and its heading indents are inconsistent (B4, B5).

A uses an elegant serif throughout with unobtrusive headings and a slim top rule. Text flows continuously through pages 2-4, so the pages are evenly filled. B has heavy header and footer bands and numbered headings in a sans face. Its page 2 ends with a gap, page 5 is mostly empty with one short paragraph, and the figure is stranded on its own page. That makes B's rhythm choppy, while A's is steadier.

A has a stronger structure: navy header and footer bands on the text pages, a split-colour section divider (A4) with a large title, and a clear sans-serif hierarchy. B is plainer, with a serif body, indented text and a heading that sits outdented from the body (B4). A wastes space on the near-empty pages A3 and A7 and on the divider, while B's pages are fuller, but B's section opener is weak and the cover is a flat mid-blue. A reads as the more designed and polished document.

A uses a serif face with comfortable margins and leading, which reads like a book (A2-A4). Its headings are modest but clear, with a rule above History and a thin top line. B has stronger heading hierarchy from the History band, but its heavy header and footer bands crowd the pages and the sans body text is denser and looser (B2-B4). B's image is slightly larger (B5), but A's image page is balanced and well captioned (A5). Overall A looks more refined and is easier to read.

A keeps one consistent column with a top rule, running footer and a clear serif heading hierarchy. Its image sits well inside the text flow on A3, and pages are filled evenly. B has misaligned headings that hang outside the indented text, and drop caps whose wrapped text breaks the left edge on B4 and B5. B also leaves large empty areas on B2, B3 and B6, and the headings and rules sit unevenly at the top of pages. B's cover is fine, but its interior is less polished.

A uses drop caps and clean sans headings with a rule above the History heading. Its small running footers are quiet and give the pages an editorial feel (A2-A4). B has heavy navy header and footer bands plus numbered headings; they are consistent but make the pages look more like a template (B2-B4). Both leave page 5 mostly empty and use the same photo page, so those are equal. B's cover is a darker navy and is fine. Overall A is more refined.

B has a table of contents (B2), steady running pages with a top rule band, and images that sit with the text, so the pages are full and the flow is consistent (B4, B7). A's cover is a vivid blue and its sans headings are clean (A2, A4), but A3 is a mostly empty page holding only the image, A4 opens with a large blank gap above the heading, and A has no contents page. Those make A's rhythm and balance uneven.

B has a clear numbered heading hierarchy in a bold sans against a serif body. Its header and footer bands give running context, and its pages are filled evenly, with a larger image and tight, consistent rhythm (B3, B4). A has an elegant look, but its heading sizes are inconsistent: the lead paragraphs under the H2 headings are set larger than the body text, which reads as odd (A2, A3). A also leaves pages 4 and 5 with large empty areas at the bottom. Both designs show the same broken image markdown on the last page.

A has a clear hierarchy: a running header band with the section name, a filled band for the Precursors heading, and bold sans subheads that stand out from the body. A also fits the content into 4 pages with a steady flow. B's Precursors heading is weak and looks like body text, its header is only a thin rule, and its last page is nearly empty apart from the broken image markup. Both show the same broken image text, and A's justified text has some wide gaps, but B's serif body is readable and pleasant.

A starts each section on a fresh page with a rule and a sans heading, and the Precursors intro is set off in larger type (A3). Its H2 headings are clearly distinct and its running footers change with the section. B uses a uniform running header and numbered headings, but its text is dense and cramped, and the sections flow together without clear breaks (B3, B4). Both leave the broken image markdown on the last page (A5, B5). B's markdown line is justified with wide gaps, which looks worse. A's covers are similar in quality.

A pairs a serif body with sans headings and numbered sections (1, 2, 2.1). Its heading hierarchy is clear and the running headers show the current section. Its text is comfortable to read, and the image sits well on A3. B uses full-width navy band headings, which are heavy. It strands the 'Etymology' heading at the bottom of B2 with the section split across pages. Its light sans body is thinner and less readable, and B5 is left half empty. Both designs share the broken image markdown text, so that does not separate them.

A reads as a more polished, consistent document. Its serif headings and body are cohesive, a top rule band frames each page, and the text flows to full pages (A2-A4) before the image page. B has a heavier sans heading style with drop caps. The drop caps are misaligned with the text, headings sit outside the text margin (B2), and the near-empty page B5 leaves a large dead area. B's cover is a flat mid-blue, which is less refined than A's dark navy cover.

B reads as a continuous serif document with a table of contents, a steady text flow and images placed alongside text. A has bold header and footer bands and a distinctive divider page (A4), but it leaves large empty areas: A3 holds only an image, A7 is mostly blank, and A8 has a big gap below the image. This breaks the rhythm. B's pages are fuller and more even (B3 to B7), although its heading hierarchy is weaker and it has no running header.

A has bold sans headings, drop caps and a lead-paragraph/body size contrast, so the hierarchy is clearer and the typography more distinctive (A3, A4, A5). The image sits directly under its section heading with a caption (A3). But A's pages end with large empty areas and uneven fills, and A4 starts with a large blank gap at the top, which hurts rhythm and balance. B flows continuously with consistent, even pages and a clean serif, but its headings are weak, sections break mid-page, and the paragraph that introduces the image is separated from its heading (B2-B3). A's typographic structure still wins slightly.

A has clear sans-serif headings, drop caps and bold section titles (A2-A4), so the structure is easy to scan. B sets headings in the same serif as the body, and its text pages run continuously with little differentiation (B2-B4). A's weakness is rhythm: A5 is mostly empty, with a short orphaned text block, and the headings sit in a left margin that doesn't align with the body text. B's pages are consistently filled. The cover and image pages are comparable. Overall A's stronger hierarchy and typography outweigh its page-fill flaw.

A has navy header and footer bands with running titles and 'Page X of 6', numbered headings, and a consistent text block that gives it a coherent system (A2-A4). B has no bands. Its drop caps are decorative but inconsistent: the intro text sits at a different indent from the rule, the heading is off the margin, and the drop-cap indents look awkward (B2-B4). Both leave page 5 mostly empty and have the same image page, but B's left margin is misaligned and the wine-press image slightly overshoots the text block (B6).

A uses a serif text face with a restrained top rule and thin dividers, so it reads as a calm editorial document with generous margins (A2, A3). Its H2 headings are larger, lighter serif and sit clearly above the smaller bold H3s (A4). B has a clear hierarchy, but its heavy navy header and footer bars and full-width heading bands feel boxy and crowd the text. B's body text is dense and small, with a sans face and wide justified gaps (B2, B4). Both designs show the same broken image markdown line on the last pages (A5, B5), and B's page 5 is half empty. The two covers are similar.

A pairs a bold sans heading face with a serif body, so the section levels are clearly separated (A3, A4). Its running footers name the section, and the indented 'Precursors' block reads well. B uses a light serif for the headings, which makes them weak, and the Precursors heading is barely distinct from the body (B3). B's body text is slightly smaller and denser, and a thick rule at the top of every page is heavy. Both leave a raw image-markdown line on the last page, and both pages are mostly empty (A5, B5). B's dark cover is more restrained, but A's blue cover is fine.

A has clear numbered sans headings in bold, so the heading levels stand out from the serif body (A2, A3, A4). Its navy header and footer bands carry the section name and page number, which helps navigation. But A leaves page 5 mostly empty and has uneven bottom whitespace, so its page rhythm is weaker (A5). B fills its pages evenly and its serif is elegant. Its headings are small, close in size to the body and weakly differentiated, and it has no running section labels (B2, B3). The page-wide fill in B is steadier, but A's hierarchy and navigation matter more.

Design A puts the lead paragraphs on page 2 and the section heading after them. Its filled navy heading bars give clear section breaks, and its subheads are cleanly bolded. Its image is wider and has a better caption. However, the sans body text is light, with tight justified lines. Page 5 is half empty, and the broken markdown image text appears in both designs. Design B uses a serif body that reads comfortably, with numbered headings that give a clear hierarchy. Its pages are fuller and more evenly filled. Because B's spacing and rhythm are more even, the page flow is smoother. The heading bars in A are stronger as bands, but B reads better overall. I give B a slight preference.

A uses a serif body with clear numbered headings (1 Precursors, 1.1, 1.2). It also has a running header rule and 'Page x of 5' footers, and its darker navy cover looks stronger (A1, A3, A4). B's headings are unnumbered, and the 'Precursors' intro is set larger and more widely spaced than the text that follows, which breaks the rhythm. It also has a stray rule at the top of B3 and looser line spacing (B3, B4). Both show the same broken image markdown on the last page (A5, B5).

A has a table of contents (A2), numbered headings, and a serif body that reads well. Its section divider carries a large '2' above the title (A5). B has a clean sans body and a larger bee photo on its last page (B8), but its headings are unnumbered and it has no contents page. B's page 7 is mostly empty, and its body text is slightly cramped. A also has big empty areas, notably A4 and A8, and it cuts off before the Eastern honey bee photo that B includes.

A pairs a serif body with clear heading levels, adds a dotted-leader table of contents, and flows text and images continuously, so its pages are well filled. B has a strong section-divider page and header/footer bands, but it leaves pages largely empty (B3 holds only an image, B7 only a few paragraphs). Its running header says 'Etymology and name' on pages where that no longer applies. Its sans-serif body is also less comfortable for long reading.

A has a navy header and footer band on every page and a solid History banner, so the structure is clear (A2). Its text pages are filled consistently, and the layout runs to five pages with the image placed well (A5). B has a stronger serif body and drop caps, but the History heading is misaligned with the body text indent (B2). B also has a nearly empty page 5 with a short orphan paragraph (B5), and the image sits on its own page afterwards. B's pagination is weaker overall.

A has strong bands, a chapter divider and numbered headings, but it wastes pages. A4 holds only an image with a large empty area below it, A5 is a section divider page, and A8 is half empty. This gives an uneven rhythm and a document that stretches to 9 pages. B flows continuously with consistent text density, and the serif type is elegant. Its two images are placed well (B4, B7), and the TOC is tidy. B's headings are lighter and less distinct than A's, but the overall reading experience is better.
